messages:
Sam P: FYI: Medicore security questionnaire flagged a KMS/HSM requirement—they require keys stored in an HSM. We're mid-POC and they ask for exception options.
Irene C: Can you paste the exact questionnaire text? most SIG items reference 'hardware root of trust' etc.
Sam P: Q: "Are customer encryption keys protected by an HSM or FIPS 140-2 level 3 equivalent?" They marked 'required' and want proof for compliance review.
Ben R: quick context: Medicore is a healthcare SaaS (PHI). They're evaluating Dedicated or Private. This is a blocker for go/no-go.
Alice M: We've discussed two paths: 1) Private deployment with customer-managed HSM, 2) Hosted + compensating controls and written exception with legal/infosec signoff.
Sam P: They prefer hosted but can't accept no-HSM. Is there an intermediate offering? e.g., customer KMS via GW or bring-your-own-key?
Irene C: Options:
- Offer BYOK via customer KMS (Cloud KMS/HSM) with key wrapping so keys never in Redwood plaintext.
- For hosted w/out HSM: apply compensating controls: dedicated tenant, strict ACLs, key access audit, quarterly key rotation, 24/7 monitoring, and contract addendum.
Ben R: Do we have any precedent where we accepted this with extra controls? I recall a pharma POC last year.
Irene C: Yes, we did a documented exception for "Phoria Health" — required: dedicated VPC, customer-supplied KMS, managed access reviews, continuous logging to customer's SIEM, and attestation.
Legal - Maya: For any exception we need: 1) risk acceptance memo, 2) contractual CL (KPI for key handling), 3) liability carveouts. We'll draft but need security's risk rationale.
Sam P: Medicore asked for timeline—POC deadline next Tuesday. Fast path would be :
- Offer temporary dev key in customer KMS + paper exception for prod
- Start private deployment eval in parallel
Irene C: Proposed compensating controls for prod exception (if customer refuses HSM):
- Customer-managed KMS for wrapping keys
- Dedicated tenant nodes, no multi-tenant key storage
- Strict role-based key access (RBAC) and JIT temporary privileges
- Syslog forwarding + immutable audit trail to customer's SIEM
- Weekly key access review and quarterly penetration test
- Contractual SOC2 + annual attestation
Ben R: Sounds reasonable. Who signs off risk?
Irene C: I'll prepare risk acceptance document and send to Zoe (CISO) and CTO for approval.
security-bot: Incident/Baseline check: no open incidents related to key leakage in last 24 months for prod clusters.
Alice M: I'll prototype the BYOK flow with KMS keywrap sample config:
```
redwood_kms:
  provider: google_cloud_kms
  key_ring: projects/medicore/locations/global/keyRings/redwood
  key_name: wrap-key
```
Sam P: Medicore: noted the controls and asked for a written risk acceptance and technical appendix by EOD tomorrow.
Irene C: I'll have draft risk memo + compensating controls checklist by EOD. tagging @Zoe (CISO) for expedited review.
Zoe (CISO): I'll review and, if controls map correctly and Legal signs the addendum, I'm comfortable to accept residual risk for prod under the listed compensating controls. Final signoff after I see the memo.
Legal - Maya: I'll prepare the contract language and send to Medicore PM. Need the security memo to attach.
Sam P: Thanks everyone — I'll update Medicore and push the BYOK config to the demo stack.
Irene C: Putting a blocker label on the sales deal until signoff — will follow up in the thread.
Ben R: +1. Keep me posted.
Zoe (CISO): Approved in principle. Formal approval pending memo + legal language. :thumbsup:
